'''Nitya Anand''' (1 January 1925 – 27 January 2024) was an Indian medicinal chemist who was the director of [[Central Drug Research Institute]] in [[Lucknow]] from 1974 to 1984.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Indian Fellow">{{cite web | url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N70-0529 | title=Indian Fellow | publisher=INSA | date=2016 | access-date=13 May 2016}}</ref> In 2005, [[Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission]] (IPC) appointed him chairman of its scientific committee. In 2012, he was awarded the [[Padma Shri]] by the Indian government.<ref name="Padma Awards">{{cite web | url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf | title=Padma Awards | publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India | date=2015 | access-date=21 July 2015 | archive-date=19 October 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171019215108/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Nitya Anand was born in [[Faisalabad|Lyallpur]], [[Punjab Province (British India)|Punjab Province]], [[British India]] on 1 January 1925. He earned his Bachelor's of Science degree from the [[Government College University, Lahore|Government College University Lahore]] in 1943 and his Master's degree in chemistry from [[St. Stephen's College, Delhi|St. Stephen's College]] in 1945. In 1948, Anand was awarded a Ph.D. in organic chemistry from the [[Institute of Chemical Technology]] in [[Mumbai]]. He received his second Ph.D. from [[St John's College, Cambridge|St. John's College]] at [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge University]]. He was a post-doctoral researcher at [[Harvard Medical School]] in 1958.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Gupta |first=A. K. Saxena; C. M. |title=A Tribute to Prof. Nitya Anand |journal=Arkivoc |year=2004 |volume=2005 |issue=2 |pages=1–8 |doi=10.3998/ark.5550190.0006.201|hdl=2027/spo.5550190.0006.201 |doi-access=free |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Indian Fellow" />

== Career ==
Anand joined [[Central Drug Research Institute]] in [[Lucknow]] in Medicinal Chemistry Division in 1951 and later became director of the Institute. Anand was chairman of Ranbaxy Science Foundation (RSF). His overall research interest has always been in the design, discovery and development of new drugs using synthetic chemistry approaches. This mainly involved consideration of factors such as drug-receptor interaction and metabolism in drug design. He published over 400 research articles and held over 130 patents. He was joint author with Jasjit S. Bindra Ph.D. of the book "Art in Organic Synthesis" which was published in 1969.<ref name=":0" /> Anand was also a Fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Indian Fellow" />

== Death ==
Anand died on 27 January 2024, at the age of 99.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr Nitya Anand, man who discovered India's first oral contraceptive pill 'Saheli', dies at 99 |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/trends/dr-nitya-anand-man-who-discovered-indias-first-oral-contraceptive-pill-saheli-dies-at-99-12136341.html |access-date=28 January 2024 |publisher=Money Control |date=28 January 2024}}</ref>
